title: How Does a Microwave Actually Heat Food?

shots.name: Cold meal enters
shots.narration: Your microwave doesn't heat the air. So what's heating your food?
shots.visual: Cold soup bowl (mist-blue tint) slides into a flat front-on microwave; door shuts. A small thermometer icon in the oven air stays low.
shots.transition: Camera pushes into the side panel, which begins to peel away.

shots.name: Cutaway: magnetron
shots.narration: This part turns electricity into microwaves — a kind of radio wave.
shots.visual: Cutaway with ghosted ivory oven outline. Neutral ivory power line pulses into the magnetron, shown as a simple labelled box; a teal wave leaves it and travels down a short channel into the oven.
shots.transition: Follow the teal wave out of the channel into the oven space (match on motion).

shots.name: Bouncing in the oven
shots.narration: They bounce around the metal box and into your food.
shots.visual: Side view. Teal waves bounce off the metal walls; a few paths cross the bowl. Where they enter the soup they fade gradually as they go in, not stopping at the surface.
shots.transition: Zoom into the soup; scale bar ticks from cm to nm.

shots.name: The waves tug water molecules
shots.narration: Water molecules have positive and negative ends. The waves tug them back and forth, billions of times a second.
shots.visual: Close-up. A few V-shaped water molecules, one marked + and −. Teal arrows show the wave pull switching direction; molecules twist part-way to follow, lagging and out of sync, never neat full spins.
shots.transition: Twisting gets crowded and messy; continuous into SH05.

shots.name: Energy becomes heat
shots.narration: All that tugging and bumping turns the waves' energy into heat. The waves reach partway in — heat spreads the rest of the way.
shots.visual: Close-up continues while background warms navy to ivory: tugged molecules knock into neighbors and tidy back-and-forth becomes random jiggling; a thermometer icon rises. Pull back to soup cross-section: teal waves enter and fade within a thick outer zone, which warms to orange as a soft band with real depth (not a thin skin); then the centre slowly warms as heat spreads inward.
shots.transition: Cross-section tilts flat into a top-down view of the oven floor.

shots.name: Hot spots and the turntable
shots.narration: Some spots get stronger waves, so the turntable keeps food moving. Still — give it a stir.
shots.visual: Top-down. Irregular brighter and dimmer teal areas mark stronger and weaker waves. Plate sits still ~2 s and heats in patches (orange beside mist blue). Turntable rotates; food passes through brighter and dimmer areas; patches soften but a few cooler spots remain. A spoon icon gives one quick stir. Areas drawn irregular, no exact spacing.
shots.transition: Turntable slows; cut to front view as the door swings open.

shots.name: Payoff
shots.narration: Waves in, hot food out — and nothing radioactive left behind.
shots.visual: Door opens; hot bowl slides out with soft steam curls while the last line plays. Small teal wave icon turns into a thermometer that keeps rising. The oven fades away and the view pushes in slowly, settling on the steaming bowl as the final frame.
shots.transition: End on the steaming bowl (no end card).
